_comment: buoy_v16.engine (MHSeals V16, YOLOv11, 13 classes) -> canonical labels. Left-hand names are VERIFIED against `YOLO(engine).names` on the Jetson, 2026-08-05, and are listed in model-index order (0..12) so this file can be diffed against that output directly. null = drop at source; nothing is dropped here on purpose — every class the model emits is a physical object, and losing an obstacle is worse than carrying a coarse label (CLAUDE.md objective 1). Detector refuses to start on an unmapped class, so a stale list after a retrain fails loudly, not silently.
_comment_red_green: The three red and three green variants collapse to one canonical label each. That reproduces the operational gate_navigator's RED_CLASSES={red_buoy,red_pole_buoy,red_light_buoy} / GREEN_CLASSES={green_buoy,green_pole_buoy,green_light_buoy} sets exactly — this repo's gate_navigator matches on the single canonical label instead of a three-name set.
_comment_blue: UNRESOLVED (Mission 1): the model has ONE blue class, but Mission 1 needs FLASHING blue (entry buoy) distinguished from SOLID blue (exit buoy). That is a temporal distinction a single-frame detector cannot make, so blue_buoy is mapped to buoy_flash_blue as a placeholder and buoy_solid_blue is currently unreachable from perception. Do NOT build entry/exit circling on this label until the G2 retrain splits the class or a flash-state classifier is added downstream.
_comment_misc: misc = 'real object, not a gate marker' — it reaches the occupancy grid and APF as an obstacle. Signs (black_cross, black_triangle) and target boats are mapped here rather than to null so they still block. Note dock_green/dock_red are NOT reachable from this model: it has no dock-bay classes, so Mission 3 bay identification cannot come from this engine as trained.
